title: Check yourself: what the compiler and andThen decide

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, when does `printer.andThen(null)` fail?

options.text: At the call that builds the chain, before any input arrives
options.says: The page says andThen throws NullPointerException at call time, not at accept time.

options.text: At the first accept on the chain, once an input arrives
options.says: The page stresses that the exception comes at call time, not at accept time.

options.text: At compile time, since null cannot stand for a Consumer
options.says: The code compiles; the page shows a NullPointerException thrown when the method runs.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens to `int count = 0; list.forEach(item -> count++);`?

options.text: It runs, and count ends up equal to the list's size
options.says: The page marks this line as a compilation error, so it never runs.

options.text: It runs, but count is still zero after the loop
options.says: The page marks this line as a compilation error, so it never runs at all.

options.text: It is rejected, since the lambda changes a captured local
options.says: The page says a captured local must be effectively final, so modifying it is a compilation error.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: andThen rejects a null consumer at the moment it is called, not later at accept time.
A lambda may only capture effectively final locals, so incrementing a captured int does not compile.
